newsitem.title: UK: EMI figures music to analysts' ears.
newsitem.headline: EMI figures music to analysts' ears.

text.p: EMI Group Plc, which on Tuesday released maiden interim results following its demerger from Thorn Plc, impressed analysts with its resilience in a patchy global music market.

"What we have seen from their competitors was poor but EMI is insulated as it does not have so much exposure to the U.S.," said Lorna Tilbian of Panmure Gordon. "They tend to be strong in the areas where the growth is coming through," she added.
Panmure is forecasting full-year profits before tax of 403 million stg, excluding any exceptional items. They have a target EMI share price of 1360p, against Tuesday's level of 1281-1/2p.
EMI earlier posted a nine percent rise in pre-tax, pre-exceptional profit to 112.5 million pounds for the six months to September 30.

Its performance compared well with rivals such as PolyGram which said last month that its full-year profits would be hit by a one-off charge of $90 million to cover costs of reorganising its music business involving 400 job losses.
The Warner Music arm of Time Warner Inc has also announced some 100 lay-offs.
EMI said that the global music market, although patchy, had continued to grow at a rate of 5.5 percent in the first half.
Turnnover from the EMI Music business was marginally lower at 1.1 billion stg but analysts ascribed this to the negative impact of currency fluctuations.
The company said album sales were 2.4 percent ahead on the previous half year while its sales of CD singles grew by almost 20 percent.
Kleinwort Benson said it was trimming its year to March 1997 pre-tax profit forecast by 10 million stg to 405 million because of the effects of the weaker yen.
But a Kleinwort analyst said the company retained its "buy" recommendation with a target price of 1485p.
Kleinwort said that the price could push up to in excess of 1620p if a bid were to emerge for EMI.
EMI has been seen as a takeover candidate following its demerger from rentals group Thorn Plc last August.
Its status as the only stand-alone music major and strong catalogue of past and present artists would make it attractive to a number of suitors.
Bid speculation helped push the shares up to around 1460p when the demerger was completed but they fell back as a bid failed to materialise.
Dennis Exton of Nikko Securities said he felt the share was fairly priced on fundamentals at current levels.
But he said he felt there should be some bid premium as a rival might seek to pounce during a period when the music market was going through a leaner period.
